subject: Hosted API threshold step-up + billing grace plan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@proserve.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API threshold step-up + billing grace plan

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on Solanchrome's projected Q3 marketing surge and the burst patterns you shared, I put together a short play to make a stepped commit increase lower friction for your engineers and procurement:

- Proposal highlights (attachment: proposed-stepup-addendum-v1.pdf)
  - 12-month step-up: increase hosted monthly commit from 250M tokens -> 600M tokens (effective 2027-07-01)
  - Billing grace: two months of soft burst credits (up to 1.2x baseline) to cover ramp volatility
  - Unit pricing: blended rate with an applied 15% volume discount for the additional commit band
  - SLO credit: operational credit (1 week of pro-rated service credit) if 95th-pct latency degradation > 30% during the first 60 days of scale

I've attached a simple usage rollforward calc (usage-rollforward-calc.xlsx) to show monthly spend scenarios and the net delta vs. pay-as-you-go. High level next steps:
1) If this looks reasonable, I'll prepare a DocuSign addendum and a short technical runbook for your infra team.
2) We can schedule a 30-min ops sync (can include Karthik) to validate rollout/runbook.

Would you like me to include the SOC2 evidence pack up front, or should I share that with procurement when you loop them?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Internal — forwarding Dana's note. They asked for a detailed cost calc and SOC2 evidence. Quick asks:

- Marissa: can you produce a short line-item with the three scenarios (60/80/110%) and the blended monthly price after 15% discount? Attach to the DocuSign packet.
- Karthik: we'll need the runbook + canary rollback checklist to include as an ops attachment (Solanchrome has a small infra team; they want confidence on rollout). Can you aim for a draft by EOD Friday?

Proposed position to negotiate with procurement if they push back: keep the 12-month effective start and guarantee the two-month soft burst as a one-time buffer tied to the step-up. If they want renewal on the buffer, we can trade that for a slightly higher initial price band.

I'll wait for the attachments and then send a cleaned proposal back to Dana + Luis.

Jordan — attaching the requested numbers and a short rationale (see usage-rollforward-calc.xlsx). Key points from ops/pricing:

- Scenario math (monthly net spend, after 15% applied to incremental band):
  - 60% utilization: $13,400/month (savings vs PAYG: ~36%)
  - 80% utilization: $17,900/month (savings vs PAYG: ~48%)
  - 110% utilization: $25,600/month (includes two months soft burst credit applied in months 1-2)

- Burst credit: recommended as a one-time two-month buffer tied to this specific step-up. If they request continuous buffer, we should price it as a recurring add-on (recommended +6.5% to blended rate).
- SLO credit language: legal okayed Priyom's suggested wording with one tiny clarification around 'sustained 24-hour window' -> we added "not caused by customer misconfiguration" exclusion.

I've attached a redline-ready PDF for DocuSign and the calc sheet. If we want to sweeten the ask, we can include a complimentary 30-minute architecture review with our infra team during onboarding.
